reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent; findings verified in-line against the tree, several reproduced by mutation in a clean clone

records.finding: The README explained the demo's `COVERAGE unavailable` line as a property of the harness. It is not: engine.Compute sets it unconditionally on every path, for every querier, so a real backend prints the same line. The ADR-0017 citation was also wrong — that ADR says CoverageLeg already carried its marker and is unchanged.
records.evidence: engine/engine.go:198-204 assigns CoverageLeg{Unavailable: ...} with no condition on the querier or any ledger; engine/coverage.go:41 Coverage() takes an explicit ledger argument and its only production call site is cmd/shortfall/reconcile.go:88.
records.reason: Rewritten in README and the demo's package doc: coverage is a reconcile-time number needing a provider ledger an impact request does not carry. The ADR-0017 citation was dropped for coverage.

records.finding: The same false attribution inside the test's own explanatory string — a comment describing adjacent code contradicted by that code.
records.reason: Rewritten to name the real cause.

records.finding: TestRunRefusesAnEmptyReport claimed to pin the guard but discarded run's exit code and asserted only that a string was ABSENT from stdout. Any failure of run leaves stdout empty and the assertion passes having inspected nothing; it never entered the guard branch.
records.evidence: Reviewer mutation: setting version 99 in demoRegistry makes registry.Parse fail, so run returns 1 with empty stdout, and the test still reported PASS.
records.reason: render() split out of run() so the guard can be entered directly. The test is now table-driven over an empty and a populated report, asserting the exit code, that stdout stays empty on refusal, and that stderr explains.

records.finding: The case asserted the bare substring "unavailable:", which three legs render (CUSTOMERS, COVERAGE, and a degraded UNREALIZED note), so it passed when the wrong leg degraded. Nothing detected a lookback regression that would silently invalidate every digit in the README block.
records.evidence: Reviewer mutation: lookbackWeeks=1 collapses the estimate to a point presented as a range and changes every figure, while the suite still reported ok.
records.reason: The assertion is anchored to "COVERAGE   unavailable:", and TestUnrealizedIsARangeNotAPoint now fails when low equals high — watched failing on that exact mutation. lookbackWeeks is also read from the parsed registry instead of restated.

records.finding: The abridgement was disclosed inaccurately: three header lines were cut, not two, and the undisclosed third was the never-add rule — the line most load-bearing for the paragraph below the fence. The customer truncation was unmentioned.
records.evidence: diff of the README fence against live output: deltas were 0a1,3 (three header lines) and 10c13,19 (seven customer rows).
records.reason: Prose now names all three cut lines individually and the truncation.

records.finding: "so you can check the report against ground truth" overclaimed: the demo prints neither the ground truth nor any reconciliation, and its only reconciliation number reads unavailable.
records.evidence: examples/demo/main.go writes only report.RenderText(rep); the omniscient checkout.Result is used solely to build the querier. Ground-truth comparison lives in testkit's goldens.
records.reason: Reworded in README and the launch message to say what the demo actually shows, and to name where ground-truth checking really happens.

records.finding: The file's own binding rule says always state pre-1.0 AND that interfaces move; the Short draft — the copy most likely to be pasted into a DM — carried only the first half.
records.reason: Short draft now carries both halves.

records.finding: "yours may differ in the last digits" understated the failure mode: a 1-ULP math.Exp difference flips a Poisson draw and adds or drops a whole transaction, changing counts, the customer list and every total.
records.evidence: examples/checkout/checkout.go poisson() derives an integer arrival count from math.Exp; testkit/cmd/genexpected warns goldens must be CI-generated for this reason.
records.reason: Reworded: not different last digits, but different counts.

records.finding: A 4,227,714-byte compiled Mach-O arm64 executable was committed at the repository root by this branch — a build artifact of `go build ./examples/demo`, tracked, unreferenced, uncovered by .gitignore, and unreviewable. On merge it would have entered git history permanently, needing a rewrite rather than a git rm to remove.
records.evidence: git ls-files -s demo -> 100755 ... ; git cat-file -s HEAD:demo -> 4227714; .gitignore covered /shortfall, cmd/shortfall/shortfall and every other built binary, but nothing matching demo.
records.reason: Removed from the index and the tree before merge, so it never entered history. /demo added to .gitignore with the reason, and the ignore verified by rebuilding and confirming git no longer sees it.

records.finding: TestUnrealizedIsARangeNotAPoint opened with a RETENTION GAP pre-guard that cannot fire: memq declares 520 weeks of history unconditionally, so engine.Unrealized's retention note never triggers here. It read as protection while providing none.
records.evidence: query/memq/memq.go:60-67 sets MetricHistoryWeeks: 520 in New; engine/unrealized.go gates the note on hw > 0 && hw < LookbackWeeks. On the real degradation the note did not appear and the test failed at the point check instead.
records.reason: Kept but relabelled honestly as a belt to the point check's braces, with a comment stating it cannot fire under the in-memory querier today and why it is still worth keeping.

records.finding: The abridgement enumeration, itself a round-1 fix, still under-described the cut by one line: it accounted for the window/version line and the never-add rule but not the report's title line.
records.evidence: Live output lines 0-2 are the title, the window line and the never-add rule; the prose listed only the latter two's contents.
records.reason: Prose now names the title line explicitly.

records.finding: A claim-table row added by the round-1 fix asserted engine.Coverage is called "only from cmd/shortfall/reconcile.go"; engine/coverage_test.go calls it nine times, and the table's stated purpose is that a reader verifies it by grepping.
records.evidence: grep 'Coverage(' engine/coverage_test.go -> 9 matches; the only non-test call site is cmd/shortfall/reconcile.go:88.
records.reason: Row now reads "only production call site".
